claims.text: The SUPPORTED margin is at least 0.10 log units per sign over the highest-scoring rival assignment.

evidence.description: Design D-03 criteria section: the SUPPORTED rule and the margins set from the originals
Phase-41 and Phase-43 margins as recorded (1.0566 to 1; +0.484 log units per token)

alternatives: A smaller margin may be adopted at outcome time if Dravidian finishes first, since finishing first is itself informative.
falsification_tests: One SUPPORTED verdict under Spec 033 issued below either condition defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A smaller margin may be adopted at outcome time if Dravidian finishes first, since finishing first is itself informative.
metadata.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED fires exactly when both conditions hold on the primary run; otherwise C11 or C12 governs the outcome.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C10 states the SUPPORTED margin condition; C15 states the SUPPORTED percentile condition; C11 states the NOT SUPPORTED rule; C12 states the INCONCLUSIVE rule. The four rules partition the outcome space and are mutually exclusive by construction; none negates another. C10 and C11 in particular do not conflict: C10's margin is measured against the best rival's score, C11's trigger is that score reaching Dravidian's, and a sub-margin Dravidian win is C12's case, not a contradiction between C10 and C11.

claims.text: Dravidian failing to finish strictly first yields NOT SUPPORTED.

evidence.description: Design D-03 criteria section: the NOT SUPPORTED rule and the status-replacement consequence

alternatives: A NOT SUPPORTED outcome may leave the inherited partial support standing, since the two methods are not comparable.
falsification_tests: One run meeting either trigger whose outcome is recorded as anything other than NOT SUPPORTED defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A NOT SUPPORTED outcome may leave the inherited partial support standing, since the two methods are not comparable.
metadata.verdict_rule: NOT SUPPORTED fires on either trigger; the status consequence of spec section 6 follows in the appended entry.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C11 states the NOT SUPPORTED rule; C10 states the SUPPORTED margin condition (a margin over the highest-scoring rival assignment); C15 states the SUPPORTED percentile condition; C12 states the remaining case. The rules partition the outcome space: Dravidian strictly first with both SUPPORTED conditions met is C10/C15's case; strictly first but sub-margin is C12's; failing to finish strictly first is C11's. C11 and C15 do not conflict: C15's percentile is a condition on SUPPORTED, and a run can fail it while finishing first (C12's case, where the range condition also lives) or fail to finish first (C11's case) — the claims govern different outcome regions and neither negates the other. Against C12: C11's region (no win) and C12's region (a sub-margin win, or the sensitivity reversal) are disjoint by construction.

claims.text: A winning margin below 0.10 log units per sign yields INCONCLUSIVE.

falsification_tests: One run meeting either trigger whose outcome is recorded as SUPPORTED or NOT SUPPORTED defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A sensitivity reversal may be reported as a caveat under a SUPPORTED verdict, since the verdict rests on the primary run.
metadata.verdict_rule: INCONCLUSIVE fires on either trigger; the sensitivity is reported with the outcome either way, and it issues no verdict of its own beyond this rule.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C12 states the INCONCLUSIVE triggers; C10 and C15 state the SUPPORTED conditions; C11 states the NOT SUPPORTED rule; the four partition the outcome space. C12's sensitivity trigger does not contradict the rule that the verdict rests on the primary run: the reversal is a primary-design condition on the verdict, declared in advance, not a second verdict. C12 and C11 are adjacent regions of one partition, distinguished by the margin: C11's region is no win at all; C12's is a win under the fixed margin (or the sensitivity reversal). The claims are consecutive cases of one rule set and neither negates the other.
